headline: Goldman Sachs forecasts the S&P 500 will rise to 8,700 over the next year, mostly because of company profits.
score_reason: Pool score 6 lowered by 1: the Goldman Sachs report was first released on 21 Sep 2026, so today's article restates an earlier forecast.
importance_line: Ordinary investors in US stock funds are told the rally rests on profits rather than inflated prices, but Goldman itself says the AI spending boost will fade and the forecast depends on AI turning into real productivity gains.
source: Financial Express, citing Goldman Sachs Research
summary: Financial Express reports that Goldman Sachs Research forecasts the S&P 500 will reach 8,700 within 12 months, about 13.5% above its 2 Oct close, driven by earnings growth rather than higher valuations. Goldman says nearly half of this year's earnings growth comes from AI investment, that this boost should fade, and that a Shiller price-to-earnings ratio above 40 is a rare warning sign.
notes: Older news: the Goldman report was first released 21 Sep 2026 (S&P 500 at 7,764 then); Financial Express re-reports it with the 2 Oct close of 7,666.45 against a record 7,816.70. Article carries a no-advice disclaimer.
